messages.author: fbff4100433066b4
messages.subject: saving plots generated by Stan
parts:
I am unable to save stan_diag plots to a file?

> p <- stan_diag(model_fit)
> ggsave(filename = 'stan_diag.pdf', plot = p)
Saving 8.52 x 6.35 in image
Error in UseMethod("grid.draw") : 
  no applicable method for 'grid.draw' applied to an object of class "list"

The pdf stan_diag.pdf saved doesn't open.

same is true for other plots like stan_ac, stan_dens etc..

messages.author: 8b5528dd7856a600
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] saving plots generated by Stan
parts:
The rstan devs will probably have a better answer, but basically stan_diag returns a list of plots, not a single ggplot object. One approach is to save each plot separately, but I’ve also sometimes used cowplot::plot_grid to combine the plots before saving:

library(cowplot)
pgrid = do.call(“plot_grid”, c(p, nrow=3)
ggsave(file=…, plot=pgrid)

—Chris

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] saving plots generated by Stan
parts:
Agreed — the error you’re getting *now* is from issue 381, but it’s a different error than before!

ggsave after plot_grid should work if you do one of:
* install the develop branch of Rstan from Github,
* or save the figure in a non-PDF format,
* or override the plot themes to use a different font… if you want to go that route, there are some examples in the issue Bob linked.
